strings.name: Beyoncé
strings.role: Singer and producer · Music, film and Black culture
strings.summary: Beyoncé moved from Destiny’s Child into a solo career that combines singing, dance, record production and visual storytelling. Visual albums such as Beyoncé and Lemonade explore relationships, Black women’s experiences and cultural memory. Renaissance and Cowboy Carter continue that inquiry through dance and country music histories. Her recordings and performances have contributed to debates about genre, cultural inheritance and women’s creative autonomy.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected musical and performance milestones cover 1981–September 2026. The Grammy total refers specifically to the 2025 ceremony.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Music and moving images
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The 2013 self-titled visual album and 2016 Lemonade organize songs, dance and film into connected narratives.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Exploring musical histories
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Renaissance engages with Black dance music and ballroom culture; Cowboy Carter explores country music and its Black cultural connections.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Grammy achievements
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Cowboy Carter won Album of the Year and Best Country Album in 2025, among other awards, bringing her total to 35 at that ceremony.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Releases B’Day’s twentieth-anniversary edition
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Issued a remastered, expanded edition, revisiting early recordings and adding material to mark her second solo album.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Cowboy Carter wins awards and goes on tour
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The album won Grammys for Album of the Year and Best Country Album; its stadium tour began that April.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Releases Cowboy Carter
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Made country music a major creative direction, combining different sounds and broadening discussion of American musical history.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Releases Renaissance
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Released a dance-focused album connecting disco, house and other Black musical traditions.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Headlines Coachella
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Became the festival’s first Black woman headliner, using a marching band and dance to reference historically Black college and university culture.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases Lemonade
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Used a visual album to connect intimate emotions, social memory and Black women’s experiences, extending music’s narrative possibilities.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Surprise-releases a self-titled visual album
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Released Beyoncé without a conventional advance promotional campaign, presenting a complete film component alongside the recording.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Begins her solo album career
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Released Dangerously in Love, moving from group membership into an independent recording career as a singer and creator.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Destiny’s Child achieves a mainstream breakthrough
strings.timeline.event-09.text: The Writing’s on the Wall and its songs expanded the group’s audience and helped establish the basis of her subsequent solo career.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Houston
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Houston, Texas; she later entered professional music through group performance and recording.
strings.influence.rationale: Her albums, films and live performances broaden pop expression, connecting Black culture and women’s experiences with popular art.
